driver: Each unit's capacity-schedule tier depends on a short-interval, two-component, worst-channel peak hidden behind three coupled observation processes: sub-unit peak registers lack timestamps and cluster labels so latent cross-feeder synchronization must be recovered from hourly residuals after stripping regional diurnal-weather factors and combined in correlated quadrature; the orthogonal component cancels opposite-signed flows in monthly net registers while upstream supply voltages are metered only at regional supply points so all units sharing a radial corridor must be solved simultaneously through shared line and transformer impedances demeaned against monthly net totals; and partial sub-unit telemetry passes its own commissioning audit at 100% while hiding opposite channel skew in the unmetered legacy pool, requiring total channel share inversion from load-driven differential bus voltage sag.
driver_concrete: Each substation's 2027-2029 relief schedule tier depends on its peak 15-minute limiting-phase apparent load (MVA), reconstructed by (1) stripping four regional diurnal-weather SVD modes from hourly feeder SCADA to isolate pairwise feeder innovation correlation R_ij (distinguishing synchronized clusters from staggered feeders of identical class) and combining monthly feeder 15-minute excesses in correlated quadrature calibrated on four modernized reference sites, (2) solving coupled radial 66 kV sub-transmission corridor impedance linear systems from GSP-Nord and GSP-Sor through shared 66 kV line impedances and local LTC taps jointly demeaned against monthly net kVARh, and (3) inverting total heaviest-phase load share from the PT-free load-driven 3-phase LV bus voltage-sag slope calibrated on the four modernized sites' 3-phase main-bay PQ archive rather than drifted GIS tags or partial 20/36 AMI telemetry.
stump: Careful solvers use hourly SCADA or pooled/class-OLS diversity factors (missing latent feeder synchronization), net kVARh / class PFs / local single-site GSP voltage drop (missing coupled 66 kV corridor impedance), and GIS tags or self-confirming 20/36 AMI telemetry (missing opposite skew in the 16 non-AMI legacy laterals), misplacing three to five of seven substations and failing the 4-site blind reference check by 5.0x to 38.7x.
